newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe merchant bank seeks dual listing.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe merchant bank seeks dual listing.

text.p: Zimbabwe's first black-owned merchant bank, National Merchant Bank, said on Wednesday it would seek a dual listing on the London and Zimbabwe stock exchanges to raise some Z$400 million ($35.5 million) for its operations.

National Merchant Blank (NMB) managing director Julius Makoni said in a statement the bank would seek the bulk of investment from foreigners who currently account for four percent of the group's capital base.
He said the local exchange was too small to solely take up the whole flotation of shares and that listing on the London bourse would translate into a better share price.
"The bank will receive more foreign currency...by listing on the LSE than it would through other means," Makoni said.

The NMB boss said the bank wanted to increase its capital base to take advantage of new business opportunities coming up in Zimbabwe with the continued liberalisation of the southern African country's economy

NMB deuty managing director James Mushore told Reuters the shares would be floated on March 26, with the offer closing on April 9. He said both listings were set for mid April, adding that the share price was yet to be determined at a later date.
